#+title: Run checks through Nix

Nix recipes describe SDKs, native providers and bounded qualification workers.
The client configuration selects a local worker or a remote build provider.
Checks consume an immutable source snapshot and return small text receipts.

* Run selected files

Use a client with Nix and a configured worker. The
[[../../nix/artifact-host.nix][artifact host module]] can configure an SSH builder, pinned host key and
daemon-owned credentials. Existing standard Nix configuration works too.

#+begin_src sh
scripts/ci-check --sdk /absolute/retained-sdk-selection \
  --out .local/checks/core \
  test/bl/core_dotimes_test.bl test/bl/core_switch_test.bl
#+end_src

The SDK selection is an actual immutable Nix product. The command captures
Git-visible source files, including current edits, and refuses changes during
capture. Repository-local file links are materialized into the snapshot.
Each request runs in a bounded VM with a real user manager, 6 GiB RAM,
2 CPUs, no swap and a 24 GiB scratch disk. The command honors configured Nix
routing. =--remote= disables local Nix workers for this request; =--local=
allows one local worker. Ordinary CI calls use the configured policy.

Select one partition of the ordinary bounded inventory with:

#+begin_src sh
scripts/ci-check --sdk /absolute/retained-sdk-selection \
  --out .local/checks/shard-0 --shard 0 --shards 4
#+end_src

Use =--source /path/to/another/checkout= to capture another tree. Every output
directory must be absent so earlier receipts remain inspectable.

Ordinary test files have a 300-second worker bound. The isolation inventory
=scripts/test-isolation.json= can declare a stress file as an object with
=reason= and =timeout_seconds= (at most 1800 seconds). That file gets its own
process and the declared finite bound; other files keep the ordinary bound.
Process receipts record the applied timeout. The forty-release evolution
stress case uses 1200 seconds while retaining each transition's public deadline.

Tests that declare Nix tools in =scripts/test-prerequisites.json= need a real
registered store and daemon: their synthetic native crates cannot be built in
the worker's read-only shared store. The host lane discovers every file with
those declared prerequisites. Hosted CI runs them serially in one separate
host job. The ordinary VM shards and this
host job are disjoint and together contain the complete original inventory.

On an explicitly selected host with the real daemon, user manager and configured
worker policy, run that lane with:

#+begin_src sh
nix-build nix/ci-release-runtime.nix -o .bl/ci-release-runtime
scripts/ci-host-nix-check --local --sdk /absolute/retained-sdk-selection \
  --out .local/checks/host-nix
#+end_src

The host qualifier has a real 6 GiB cgroup cap, zero swap and a finite deadline.
The pinned loader adapter runs inside that manager unit. The native producer
retains its existing bounded Nix VM; Nix clients honor the host's configured
worker policy. A client can route native builds to a private station or
nixbuild.net while executing the host qualifier locally.
No nested daemon, writable store overlay or unsandboxed native recipe is used.
Both lanes share source capture, exact SDK/candidate verification and per-file
receipts. Explicit requests for these files through the bounded VM client fail
before a VM starts.

* SDK production and reuse

=--sdk= consumes an existing selection. Without it, the check depends on the
ordinary SDK recipe. =--previous= supplies a retained predecessor whose
validated namespace units can be reused. Requests with the same production
inputs use the same Nix SDK dependency.

SDK metadata is read inside the worker. A thin client can evaluate the normal
recipe without first fetching its completed SDK. Persistent runner policy
must retain the qualified predecessor and its unit store across revisions;
ordinary test-source edits can reuse the existing selection directly.

* Read the result

=result.json= records status, selected files, assertion count, frozen-source
identity, SDK descriptor digest, candidate digest and compiler floor digest.
=files.jsonl= contains per-file outcomes; =run.log= contains test diagnostics.

Physical Nix store roots in returned text become stable opaque SHA-256 labels.
Content digests remain intact. The output has =outputChecks.out.allowedReferences = []=;
unexpected store dependencies make Nix refuse publication. SDK links, binary
payloads and oversized text exports are refused.

A failed test produces an inspectable receipt and the client exits nonzero.
The client requires a passing result for its exact request, unchanged inputs,
nonzero assertions and complete identities. With an explicit SDK, its actual
descriptor digest must also match.

* GitHub Actions

The =nix-worker= action selects one backend through the repository variable
=NIX_BUILD_BACKEND=:

- =local= (default): one local Nix worker with verified KVM access.
- =configured=: the client's existing Nix builder and SSH configuration.
- =nixbuild=: the pinned official nixbuild.net action configures builders,
  authentication and substitution. Set the repository secret =NIXBUILD_TOKEN=
  to a token with =build:read=, =build:write=, =store:read= and =store:write=.
  Local Nix workers are disabled. Missing credentials fail before production.

=CI_RUNNER= and =CI_PRODUCER_RUNNER= select runner labels; the default is
=ubuntu-24.04=. Nix recipes contain no runner labels or provider credentials.
The nixbuild backend requires KVM on its remote x86_64 worker, not on the CI
runner. The host qualifier uses Linux, a real Nix store and a systemd user
manager. The action provisions that user manager independently of the backend.

[[https://docs.nixbuild.net/kvm-builds/][nixbuild.net KVM support]] requires =kvm= in the worker derivation's
=requiredSystemFeatures=. The bounded worker supplies that requirement.
[[https://github.com/nixbuild/nixbuild-action/tree/ccd11ee76c26c018e8470835dc2e286a5a024a14][The pinned provider action]] supplies builder features and private client configuration.
The coordinator and bootstrap wrappers preserve those settings across managed
process boundaries. Product identity and verification use the same recipes
for every backend.

Store-only providers realize derivations remotely with evaluation on the
client. The optional station evaluation endpoint is a separate capability;
CI using nixbuild.net does not require it. Provider activation needs a run
with real account credentials to qualify that deployment.

The cheap CI gate evaluates local, externally configured and SSH-service module
policies. The SDK gate exercises current client Source in a fresh private
compiler world and checks exact operator environment forwarding. The Python
controls execute the generated coordinator wrapper across a separate manager
environment, including absent settings and literal dollar characters.

The Nix-aware Actions cache retains the registered SDK closure, validated
namespace units, pinned model assets and immutable engine source hint across
clean checkouts. Consumers require the producer's exact selector and cache;
they do not start a replacement producer after a cache miss. Rolling releases
consume the successful main CI run's candidate and commit identity.

The three CI-only recipes =ci-check.nix=, =ci-release-runtime.nix= and
=ci-sdk-gates.nix= are excluded from engine capture and its fingerprint. Editing
these checks does not select another SDK. Cache restore also recognizes the
immediately preceding policy that included exactly these files, preserving its
original engine identity as a predecessor. Current preparation and qualification
selectors still require the current engine fingerprint.

Model provisioning calls the selected Nix-linked SDK's =bin/bl --cold install
embed= directly. =ci-model-input.py provision= requires a successful process and
verifies every pinned file and the completion digest before retaining a model
input. Portable runtime acceptance remains a separate gate on the exact release
candidate.

The canonical compiler recipe prepares generation P, produces B from P and C
from B, and runs =check-source-floor= in a fresh VM for each generation. It
requires identical complete B/C byte inventories before installing C. CI uses
=scripts/check-produced-compiler.py --sdk .bl/sdks/current-sdk= to verify the
registered immutable proof, every installed compiler seed byte and the SDK
image's exact matching floor. This check starts no VM or compiler. The committed
bootstrap floor is a predecessor input; it need not equal the produced C floor.

Builder keys remain host-owned files; provider tokens are CI secrets. Runner
labels select orchestration capacity, while Nix configuration selects builders.
